Docs: MDN — Using promises — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Using_promises

notes.quote: A fetch() promise only rejects when the request fails, for example, because of a badly-formed request URL or a network error. A fetch() promise does not reject if the server responds with HTTP status codes that indicate errors (404, 504, etc.).

notes.back:
all: boom
allSettled: fulfilled,rejected

Why: Promise.all rejects with the first rejection. Promise.allSettled always fulfills, with a status for each promise. Neither one starts the work: the promises were already running when created.

Docs: MDN — Promise.all() — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise/all
notes.quote: It rejects when any of the input's promises rejects, with this first rejection reason.
